Sure, here are two hints for the given problem:

Hint 1: Consider the nature of the data and the problem of overfitting. Overfitting occurs when a model learns the noise in the training data rather than the actual signal. Regularization techniques can help mitigate this by penalizing certain model parameters.

Hint 2: Think about the characteristics of L1 and L2 regularization. L1 regularization tends to produce sparse models by driving some coefficients to zero, which can be beneficial when dealing with redundant features. L2 regularization, on the other hand, tends to shrink coefficients but does not necessarily make them zero.
